newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish state budget sees lower 1996, 1997 deficits.
newsitem.headline: Danish state budget sees lower 1996, 1997 deficits.

text.p: Denmark predicted falling state budget deficits for 1996 and 1997 in forecasts contained in its 1997 draft budget unveiled on Tuesday.

It saw a 1996 deficit of 31.0 billion crowns, compared to a May government forecast of 31.1 billion and an actual 1995 deficit of 31.2 billion. It expected a 1997 shortfall of 22.6 billion crowns, down from 30.0 billion crowns predicted earlier.
The new figures represented 3.1 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in 1996 and 2.2 percent in 1997. The budget deficit has fallen every year since 1994.
Finance Minister Mogens Lykketoft said his 1997 budget proposal implied "a moderately restrictive stance corresponding to a fiscal effect of -0.5 percent of GDP.
The draft, which has yet to be ratified by parliament, set 1997 state expenditure at 388.7 billion crowns and revenue at 366.1 billion crowns.

After negotiations between the Social Democrat-led centre-left minority coalition government and opposition parties this autumn, parliament is expected to pass the budget in December. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
